findings.title: Roo Code privileged GitHub Actions workflow RCE
findings.summary: NVD updated CVE-2025-58371 for Roo Code, an AI-powered autonomous coding agent, where versions 3.26.6 and below used unsanitized pull-request metadata in a privileged GitHub Actions context, enabling remote command execution on the runner, repository modification, secret access, and malicious release or package creation. The record says version 3.26.7 fixes the issue.
findings.evidence_classification: vulnerability-advisory; updated-in-window; public database plus vendor advisory and patch references
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Coding-agent projects often ship privileged automation around generated code and extension releases. This record is a concrete repository supply-chain compromise path for an AI coding-agent ecosystem component.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad Roo Code product/entity background belongs upstream.
General coding-agent CI/release governance practice belongs upstream; this repository should keep the security-specific supply-chain finding.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for affected versions and fix because NVD, GitHub advisory, and patch references align. Treat the in-window qualification as an NVD update, not first disclosure.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, check whether a local Roo Code security leaf already exists before creating a duplicate.
Reconcile whether the durable home is infrastructure-and-supply-chain or agent-and-tool-security based on existing page granularity.

findings.title: mcp-kubernetes-server chained-command write/delete guard bypass
findings.summary: NVD updated CVE-2025-59376 for feiskyer mcp-kubernetes-server through 0.1.11. The server's --disable-write and --disable-delete checks consider only the first command word, allowing chained commands such as a read-like first command followed by a delete operation.
findings.evidence_classification: vulnerability-advisory; updated-in-window; public database plus code reference
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP servers that mediate Kubernetes access must enforce least privilege at final command execution, not only at initial tool selection or first-token parsing.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad MCP server cataloging belongs upstream.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for the control-bypass fact from NVD and referenced source code. Fixed version was not identified in the fetched record.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, check for a patch or release note after 0.1.11.
Compare with existing final-query authorization and MCP command-policy pages.

findings.title: ADB MCP Server command injection in tool implementation
findings.summary: NVD updated CVE-2025-59834 for ADB MCP Server versions 0.1.0 and prior, where MCP tool definitions and implementation are vulnerable to command injection. The record points to commit 041729c as the patch.
findings.evidence_classification: vulnerability-advisory; updated-in-window; public database plus GitHub advisory and patch
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An MCP server that bridges agent calls to Android Debug Bridge can turn tool arguments into device or host command execution if it does not treat model-selected parameters as hostile input.

upstream_routing.reason: General adb-mcp entity context belongs upstream; local durable coverage should focus on command-injection boundary.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for affected boundary and patch reference. Ingest should verify whether a versioned release contains the patch.
follow_up_actions: Recheck GitHub release tags before durable synthesis.
Map to existing MCP command-injection pages if pattern-level consolidation is better than a new leaf.

findings.title: Dify plaintext API key exposure to non-admin frontend users
findings.summary: NVD updated CVE-2025-67732 for Dify before 1.11.0. The advisory says API keys are exposed in plaintext to the frontend, letting non-administrator users view and reuse keys for unauthorized access to third-party services and quota consumption. Version 1.11.0 fixes the issue.
findings.evidence_classification: vulnerability-advisory; updated-in-window; public database plus GitHub advisory reference
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: LLM application platforms frequently hold provider API keys and delegated credentials; frontend exposure breaks least privilege and can shift AI provider cost and data access to unauthorized users.

upstream_routing.reason: General LLM platform key-management practice belongs upstream; this repository keeps the vulnerability and credential-security impact.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for the security fact and fixed version from NVD. Treat as an in-window update rather than first disclosure.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, check for existing Dify or LLM credential-exposure leaves.
Preserve the third-party-service quota and delegated-credential implication.

findings.title: Firefox AI chatbot leaked prior tab title into chat prompt
findings.summary: NVD updated CVE-2025-3035, where using the AI chatbot in one Firefox tab and later activating it in another could leak the previous tab's document title into the chat prompt. Mozilla fixed the issue in Firefox 137.
findings.evidence_classification: vulnerability-advisory; updated-in-window; public database plus vendor advisory reference
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Browser-integrated AI assistants create privacy boundaries between page state and model prompts; cross-tab title leakage is a concrete prompt-context data-minimization failure.

upstream_routing.reason: Firefox and browser AI assistant product context belongs upstream.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for the fixed version and leakage boundary from NVD and Mozilla references. Publication predates the window; the qualifying date is NVD lastModified.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, connect to browser-agent runtime and data-minimization topics if not already captured.
Verify whether local docs already synthesized this older Mozilla advisory.

findings.title: Red Hat OpenShift AI guardrails and dashboard vulnerabilities updated
findings.summary: NVD updated two Red Hat OpenShift AI records. CVE-2026-15154 describes a ReDoS in guardrails-detectors where crafted regular expressions against the public detection API can drive catastrophic backtracking and deny the guardrails-mediated LLM pipeline. CVE-2026-16745 describes odh-dashboard binding behavior that lets an in-cluster actor bypass authentication and impersonate users against the Kubernetes API.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Red Hat OpenShift AI guardrails-detectors and odh-dashboard components; exact fixed builds require Red Hat advisory reconciliation
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The records affect two key AI platform controls: guardrail availability and dashboard identity enforcement. Both are release-gate concerns for hosted AI workloads.

upstream_routing.reason: OpenShift AI product/platform context belongs upstream.

findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence for vulnerability descriptions from NVD. Fixed-version detail needs Red Hat primary advisory reconciliation during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Fetch Red Hat errata or Bugzilla references during ingest to confirm fixed builds.
Route guardrails-detectors to testing-and-assurance or model-and-prompt security, and odh-dashboard to identity-and-access.

findings.title: Official MCP server-git repository boundary fixes updated
findings.summary: NVD updated official Model Context Protocol Servers records affecting mcp-server-git. CVE-2025-68143 says git_init accepted arbitrary filesystem paths and made those directories eligible for later git operations before the tool was removed. CVE-2025-68145 says --repository restrictions did not validate subsequent repo_path arguments against the configured repository, allowing operations on other accessible repositories. The records point to upgrades at or after 2025.9.25 and 2025.12.17 respectively.
findings.evidence_classification: vulnerability-advisory cluster; updated-in-window; public database plus upstream advisory index
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-server-git before 2025.9.25 for git_init removal and before 2025.12.17 for repository path validation
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Repository-scoped MCP tools must enforce filesystem and repository boundaries on every tool call. Otherwise an agent with apparent repo-limited authority can mutate or inspect neighboring repositories.

upstream_routing.reason: General official MCP server catalog entries belong upstream.
General repository-boundary practice for coding agents belongs upstream; local synthesis should keep the concrete MCP vulnerability facts.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for the affected versions from NVD text. Ingest should verify linked GitHub advisories for exact GHSA identifiers.
follow_up_actions: Delta-review against existing mcp-server-git and repository-boundary pages.
Check whether these belong as one cluster leaf or separate path-boundary leaves.

findings.title: Meta Ads MCP auth fallback and image-fetch SSRF fixes updated
findings.summary: NVD updated two Meta Ads MCP records. CVE-2026-54547 describes HTTP auth middleware that accepts any X-Pipeboard-Token value and falls back to the operator's META_ACCESS_TOKEN, causing tools to execute with operator Meta credentials. CVE-2026-54549 describes upload_ad_image fetching attacker-controlled URLs before credential validation, enabling SSRF to loopback, private networks, metadata endpoints, or redirect-chained internal targets. Both are fixed in 1.0.115.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Meta Ads MCP < 1.0.115 when streamable HTTP/server-side token deployment is used
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This cluster combines delegated advertising-account authority with unauthenticated HTTP tool access and SSRF, a concrete example of why MCP credentials and network fetch tools need independent enforcement before tool execution.

upstream_routing.reason: Meta Ads MCP entity context belongs upstream.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for vulnerability shape and fixed version from NVD. Primary repository/advisory references should be rechecked during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Route credential fallback to identity-and-access and SSRF to agent-and-tool-security, or create one cluster leaf if existing patterns favor grouped product fixes.
Confirm whether stdio-only deployments are unaffected as NVD states.

findings.title: mcp-searxng URL reader SSRF and unbounded fetch controls updated
findings.summary: NVD updated a cluster of mcp-searxng URL-reading vulnerabilities. Records cover default-disabled hardening that permits private/metadata endpoint fetches, redirect and address-classification bypasses, missing content-length enforcement that can force unbounded memory/CPU use, and DNS-resolution gaps where public-looking hostnames resolve to private or metadata addresses. Fixes are identified in versions 1.2.0 and 1.7.1 depending on the record.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-searxng before 1.2.0 for URL policy bypasses and before 1.7.1 for content-length/DNS-resolution controls
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Search and URL-reading MCP servers place model-selected URLs on a trusted server network path. These records show both confidentiality risks from internal fetches and availability risks from unbounded content ingestion.

upstream_routing.reason: mcp-searxng entity and product catalog context belongs upstream.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for cluster membership and fixed versions from NVD. Ingest should de-duplicate with any prior URL-reader SSRF leaves.
follow_up_actions: Compare with existing MCP SSRF and browser/network egress controls pages.
Preserve the distinction between default hardening-off behavior, residual bypasses, DNS rebinding, and DoS.

findings.title: MCPVault path filter bypasses for repository and Obsidian metadata
findings.summary: NVD updated two MCPVault records. CVE-2026-57441 covers case-sensitive and non-canonical path filtering that lets case variants or Windows trailing dots/spaces reach restricted .git, .obsidian, or node_modules directories on case-insensitive filesystems. CVE-2026-57442 covers root-anchored deny-list patterns that miss nested restricted segments. Fixes are identified in 0.11.4 and 0.11.5.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MCPVault < 0.11.4 and < 0.11.5 depending on bypass path
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Vault and repository MCP file tools need canonical path enforcement before read, write, move, search, and listing actions because an AI agent can be induced to select sensitive metadata paths.

upstream_routing.reason: General repository metadata and documentation-vault workflow practice belongs upstream; this repository keeps concrete path-filter failure facts.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for vulnerable behaviors and fixed versions from NVD. Verify upstream release tags during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Connect to existing MCP path traversal and file-boundary pages.
Check whether case-insensitive filesystem caveat warrants a local maintenance note.

findings.title: @zereight/mcp-gitlab unauthenticated HTTP and DNS rebinding paths updated
findings.summary: NVD updated @zereight/mcp-gitlab records. CVE-2026-61560 describes default Docker/SSE exposure of all MCP tools without authentication, including upload_markdown reading arbitrary local files and uploading them to GitLab, enabling token theft and GitLab account takeover; version 2.1.27 patches it. CVE-2026-61568 describes missing Host/Origin allow-list enforcement on Streamable HTTP, enabling DNS rebinding to a victim local MCP listener; version 2.1.30 patches it.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: @zereight/mcp-gitlab < 2.1.27 for unauthenticated SSE/file read path; < 2.1.30 for DNS rebinding host/origin control
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Developer-platform MCP servers often hold source-control tokens. These records show how transport exposure and browser-origin controls can convert local MCP listeners into account-takeover paths.

upstream_routing.reason: MCP GitLab server catalog context belongs upstream.
General source-control agent workflow governance belongs upstream; local finding covers transport/authentication vulnerability details.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for attack paths and fixed versions from NVD. Ingest should verify GitHub advisory references.

findings.title: RMCP OAuth metadata resource confusion can leak access tokens
findings.summary: NVD updated CVE-2026-63127 for RMCP, the official Rust SDK for MCP. Before 2.0.0, OAuth discovery omits or fails to confirm the RFC 9728 resource field, allowing a malicious MCP server to redirect authorization through legitimate metadata for a different MCP resource and capture the resulting token when the client sends it back.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP OAuth clients must bind tokens to the exact protected resource. Otherwise malicious servers can harvest tokens that remain valid against legitimate MCP resources.

upstream_routing.reason: RMCP SDK entity context belongs upstream.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for fixed version and resource-confusion mechanism from NVD. Primary SDK advisory should be checked during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Route to identity-and-access and link to MCP OAuth resource-binding pages.
Check whether Zscaler or MCP confirmation-token resource-binding leaves already cover the same durable concept.

findings.title: NetLicensing and Obsidian MCP unauthenticated delegated-authority paths updated
findings.summary: NVD updated two remote MCP authorization records. CVE-2026-54446 says NetLicensing MCP Server prior to 0.1.6 accepts unauthenticated /mcp requests without API-key material and falls back to the operator's NETLICENSING_API_KEY, enabling product, license, licensee, transaction, validation, and delete operations. CVE-2026-54618 says Obsidian Web MCP prior to 0.2.0 issues OAuth authorization codes and tokens without login, consent, or client authentication, allowing remote vault read, write, search, list, move, and delete operations.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: NetLicensing MCP Server < 0.1.6; Obsidian Web MCP < 0.2.0
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Both records show remote MCP services falling back to operator-level credentials or static vault tokens when caller identity is absent, directly violating delegated authority and least privilege.

upstream_routing.reason: MCP server product/entity background belongs upstream.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for authentication failure and fixed versions from NVD. Ingest should split into separate leaves if local granularity requires product-specific pages.
